title: Zinc Deficiency in Plants: Signs, Causes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: Zinc Deficiency in Plants: Signs and Fixes
metaDescription: Zinc deficiency shows on the young leaves first. See the signs crop by crop, what causes it, and the fertilizer sold here that fixes it.
excerpt: Zinc deficiency in plants starts on the young leaves and the growing tip. Zinc helps the plant make its own growth hormone, so new leaves and stems reach full size. It is part of many enzymes and helps make chlorophyll, proteins and starch. It also helps seed and grain form and ripen. Here are the signs in each crop, what brings it, how to be sure and the fertilizer that fixes it.

blocks.text: Zinc moves only a little inside the plant. So the first signs usually appear on young and middle leaves early in the season. Rice shows pale midribs at the base of young leaves along with brown blotches on the lower leaves.
Zinc deficiency symptoms

New leaves come out small, narrow and mottled, and the joints of the stem grow close together, so shoots look bunched. Corn shows a broad pale or white band on each side of the midrib, starting at the base of the leaf. In rice, dusty brown spots appear 2 to 4 weeks after transplanting, growth turns patchy, and tillering slows and maturity comes late. Bad cases kill transplanted seedlings or stop direct seeded rice from coming up.
Zinc deficiency by crop

Each crop shows it its own way. So find yours in the tables below, then open its page for the photo and the full fix, like the one for [zinc in rice](/nutrient-deficiencies/rice-nutrient-deficiency#zinc).

blocks.text: What causes zinc deficiency

Zinc shortage is common in flooded lowland rice, because long flooding and high bicarbonate keep zinc out of reach. It has been reported across Central Luzon, Cagayan, Bicol, Western Visayas and Mindanao. Calcareous soils with a pH of 7.5 or more, saline and sodic soils, peat soils and fields high in phosphorus also run short. Fields cropped three times a year, sandy or eroded soils, and cool, wet weather early in the season make it worse.
How to be sure it is zinc

Iron shortage also yellows young leaves between the veins. But zinc makes bands near the leaf base, and iron runs the full leaf length. In rice, iron toxicity, tungro and grassy stunt can look alike, so a soil and plant test settles it. A soil test for available zinc at a DA Regional Soils Laboratory predicts the need well. A leaf tissue test at tillering confirms it. In lowland rice, the MOET pots show if zinc is the missing nutrient.
How to fix zinc deficiency

Zinc sulfate is the usual material, and a typical rate for rice is 25 kg per hectare, 10 to 14 days after transplanting. Rice seedlings can also be dipped in a 2 percent zinc oxide mix for 15 to 30 minutes before transplanting. Let the soil test confirm the need, and swap some urea for ammonium sulfate, add manure and drain fields now and then.

A typical zinc sulfate spray is about 5 grams per liter of water, and rice sprays start 14 days after transplanting. Treat it as an emergency fix, because a soil dose before or at planting works better.

How to keep zinc deficiency away
Plant zinc efficient varieties and add zinc sulfate before planting on fields known to be short. Avoid heavy phosphorus, add manure, and let flooded fields drain and dry between crops.

blocks.title: Too much is a problem too
blocks.text: Very high soil zinc, above about 100 parts per million of exchangeable zinc, can poison many crops. Zinc toxicity is rare, but stop adding zinc once the soil test shows enough.

blocks.text: Zinc deficiency questions

items.q: What does zinc deficiency look like in rice?
items.a: Dusty brown spots and streaks appear on the leaves 2 to 4 weeks after transplanting. Young leaves show a pale midrib near the base. Plants stay short and patchy, tiller poorly and ripen late.

items.q: What is the best fertilizer for zinc deficiency?
items.a: Zinc sulfate is the most used source because it dissolves well and costs little. A typical rate for rice is 25 kg per hectare, 10 to 14 days after transplanting.

items.q: How do I dip rice seedlings in zinc?
items.a: Mix zinc oxide in water to make a 2 percent mix, about 20 grams per liter. Soak the seedling roots in it for 15 to 30 minutes before transplanting.

items.q: Why is zinc deficiency common in flooded rice fields?
items.a: Long flooding raises the soil pH and bicarbonate, which lock zinc away from the roots. Draining the field from time to time and adding manure help free it.
